narrative:
The 2017 Cincinnati Reds were a team caught in the awkward middle ground of a rebuilding effort that hadn't yet found its footing. They entered the year with genuine offensive firepower — 219 home runs and a respectable .762 OPS — but a pitching staff that simply couldn't hold leads, posting a bloated 5.17 ERA and surrendering 869 runs. The result was a 68-94 campaign that was never truly competitive, but not without its flashes of brilliance.

April set the tone for what the season would become: a roster full of talented individuals unable to string together consistent winning. The bullpen was particularly vulnerable, with Blake Wood and Michael Lorenzen surrendering crushing blows in high-leverage spots. Yet May offered a temporary reprieve, as Adam Duvall, Billy Hamilton, Scott Schebler, and the surprisingly clutch Zack Cozart sparked one of the team's better offensive stretches, helping Cincinnati claw to a respectable 13-15 record in what could have been a far uglier month.

June proved to be the season's true breaking point. The pitching staff collapsed under the weight of its own limitations, with Raisel Iglesias surrendering a Corey Seager grand slam and the bullpen repeatedly failing in pivotal moments. The team went 10-17, a slide that effectively buried any lingering playoff hopes. The dog days of summer brought more of the same, though Scooter Gennett's grand slam in August and José Peraza's timely double offered reminders of how compelling this offense could be on its best days. Billy Hamilton's rare power display in September added an exclamation point to an otherwise forgettable final stretch, but by then the Reds were simply playing out the string, finishing a long 68-94 season that pointed more toward 2018 than anything else.

chapters.title: Early Stumbles
chapters.description: The Reds open the year with promise but the bullpen immediately shows its cracks, surrendering critical hits in April.

chapters.title: May Sparks
chapters.description: Duvall, Hamilton, Schebler, and Cozart ignite the offense for one of Cincinnati's best months, keeping hope alive.

chapters.title: June Unravels
chapters.description: The pitching staff collapses spectacularly in June, with grand slams and late-inning disasters burying the season.

chapters.title: Midsummer Bright Spots
chapters.description: Gennett's grand slam and Peraza's clutch double highlight a rare winning August amid an otherwise lost season.

chapters.title: Playing Out the String
chapters.description: Hamilton delivers a rare power moment and the Reds close out a 68-94 season with little left to play for.
